done_when: forge migrate calls a story finished only when every Tasks row is done in the old Forge's records (.factory/stages.json and task markers); a story with a pending part is not converted as finished and gets a replan draft under .forge-migrate/replan/ like a malformed one, and the dry run says which parts are pending; a test covers a story with one pending part

findings.body: The replan condition only covers tasks with an explicitly non-done stage. When a task lacks both a completion marker and a stage record, `_tasks` adds it to `waiting` but leaves `pending` empty, so an otherwise valid story still carries over its approval instead of becoming a replan draft. The existing TIDY-UP fixture demonstrates this: its decomposition declares T2 at tests/fixtures/copied-client/client/.factory/stories/tidy-up/decomposition.json:23, but only T1 has a completion marker; tests/test_migrate.py:127–128 still expects its approval to carry over with only one of two parts done. This violates the Done-when requirement that a story with a pending part gets a draft under `.forge-migrate/replan/`. Base that decision on all unfinished task rows and update coverage for the missing-marker case.
findings.title: Not done: pending parts without completion markers must also produce a replan draft

why: forge migrate marks an active plan finished whenever its approval is on main, even when its old-Forge stages still have parts pending (myclaw's GRANTED-1 has T1 pending, yet the dry run says every part was done)
